checks: Every projected through-point halfspace at the projected mark pulls back to an ordinary ambient through-point cap at the original deepest mark. Raw cap mass is exactly preserved; an active normal in the span realizes equality.

For any projected point the balance forces at least one nonnegative signed displacement from the projected mark. Tightening that selected active cap through the point yields the upper bound at every candidate, including points outside the support.

Orthogonal Fubini gives the (d−r)-volume slice density and unchanged total. Extending a projected segment slightly past an interior point and lifting its endpoint supplies an interior preimage. Brunn–Minkowski for the perpendicular slices makes the positive root concave and the density log-concave. The r=d case is the indicator.

Ordinary cap masses are jointly continuous by null limiting cut planes. If the active normals omit zero from their convex hull, a separated direction and an own inball give uniform positive linear growth near the active set, while the compact complement retains its old positive gap. This supplies a finite positive balance after Carathéodory.

Rank one forces both orientations of a line in the active family. Those volumes sum to the whole body, so each is half. Every other opposite pair is bounded below by the same half and has the same sum, forcing all normals active.
